name: Malaysia

legalSystem.note: Common law inherited from England, alongside Syariah law in matters of personal status and a separate body of Sabah and Sarawak state law. Federal Acts are consolidated and reprinted by the Commissioner of Law Revision, and each reprint states on its cover the date it is current to. Subsidiary legislation is made as P.U. (A) and P.U. (B) instruments and is published separately from the Acts.

languageNote: Bahasa Melayu is the authoritative language of the law. The Laws of Malaysia portal publishes each Act in both a Malay and an English edition, and the English edition is a translation whose authority is subordinate: where the two differ, the Malay text governs. The register records which edition a document came from, so a row that quotes the English text is quoting a translation and says so.

jurisdictionScope.note: Every portal this profile names publishes federal law: the Laws of Malaysia, the P.U. gazette series and the federal regulators.

notHeld.note: Sabah and Sarawak keep statute law of their own, published by their State Attorney-General's Chambers, and several federal Acts do not reach them: the Employment Act 1955 applies to Peninsular Malaysia, and the two States' labour law is their Labour Ordinances.
Each State legislates on the matters the Federal Constitution gives the States, land and Islamic law among them, and publishes its Enactments itself.

instrumentTypes.note: The principal instrument, numbered in one series: Act 709 is the Personal Data Protection Act 2010. Cited by act number and section.
Orders made under an Act, gazetted in the P.U. (A) series. The largest of the three by count: an exemption, a commencement or a prescribed rate arrives as an Order.
Regulations, rules and orders made under an Act. Where an Act leaves a standard to be prescribed, the standard is here.
Rules made under an Act, gazetted in the P.U. (A) series alongside Regulations and Orders. Same tier and same force; the series is one, and the register names the three separately.

instrumentTypes.localName: Notification, P.U. (B), and regulator policy documents
instrumentTypes.note: Bank Negara policy documents and MCMC determinations bind the licensees they are issued to by force of the parent Act. This is the tier v1 collapsed into the one above, scoring central bank guidance as though it were an Act.
Personal Data Protection Department guidance and similar. Evidence of how a regulator reads a binding instrument, never the source of an obligation on their own.

A document a body published about the law rather than an instrument of it: a consultation paper, a media release, an FAQ, a landing page for an Act held in the statute book. Registered because it is real evidence of how a regulator reads an obligation, and never the source of one. Assigned where the source states neither an identifier nor a standing.

portals.name: Laws of Malaysia
portals.authority: Attorney General's Chambers, Commissioner of Law Revision
portals.notes: The portal's table of current principal Acts is published as a PDF it generates itself, and that PDF carries every Act's number, English title, consolidation date, and a link straight to the Act's own file. That is the register, taken from one official artefact. It is deliberately not taken from the portal's search feed, which now answers with an encrypted payload the page decrypts using a key it ships to the browser: reading that would make the register depend on a key one rotation away from silently returning nothing, which is how a predecessor of this system quietly stopped enumerating Malaysia altogether. Subsidiary legislation is not reachable this way -- its links are signed with a digest we cannot compute -- and is recorded as an open gap rather than a quiet absence.

portals.name: Laws of Malaysia -- subsidiary legislation, P.U. (A)
portals.authority: Attorney General's Chambers, Commissioner of Law Revision
portals.notes: Orders, regulations and rules made under an Act. The customs prohibition and duty orders, and the anti-dumping orders, are here and not in the principal Acts.

portals.name: Laws of Malaysia -- subsidiary legislation, P.U. (B)
portals.authority: Attorney General's Chambers, Commissioner of Law Revision
portals.notes: Notifications: appointments, commencements, and the tariff and exemption notices made by notification rather than by order.

portals.name: Personal Data Protection Department
portals.notes: The Act's subsidiary regulations and the sectoral codes of practice registered under it, which is where the operative detail of Malaysia's data protection regime sits. The pages that carry the codes are built client-side, so nothing is reachable by following links; the site runs WordPress and advertises its own read-only API, and the whole document library is enumerable through it. Uploads are filed under filename slugs, so a code enters the register under a provisional title and takes its real one from the first page of the document.

portals.name: Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission
portals.notes: Determinations, guidelines and the Content Code made under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. Binding on licensees through standard licence conditions rather than on their own terms, so a row citing one has to say what makes it binding.

portals.name: National Cyber Security Agency
portals.notes: The Cyber Security Act 2024 and the codes of practice for national critical information infrastructure entities made under it.

portals.name: Bank Negara Malaysia
portals.notes: Policy documents, the technology risk management one among them, binding on financial institutions. A policy document is not an Act, and treating it as one is a mistake this profile's instrument ranking exists to prevent.

portals.name: Royal Malaysian Customs Department
portals.notes: Customs procedure and the electronic declaration systems the trade facilitation pillars turn on. Publishes in Malay by default.

portals.name: Malaysian Investment Development Authority
portals.notes: Investment guidelines and the equity conditions attached to manufacturing and services licences.

portals.name: Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia
portals.notes: Patents, trade marks and copyright administration. Recorded as a lead rather than crawled: the site refused an automated client on every path tried by a predecessor of this system, and Malaysia's intellectual property statutes are on the Laws of Malaysia portal in any case.

portals.name: MYNIC
portals.notes: The .my registry's own eligibility policies, which are the domain name requirements. Not a government host, so a row citing it has to say what makes it authoritative.

commitments.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

notes: Malaysia is the third economy built and the hardest of the three: no API, the law served as PDFs, an authoritative language that is not English, and a statute book whose subsidiary legislation is not enumerable from the portal. It is where the non-English source path is tested for real.
